text:
Today: 2026-09-14
Platform Engineering weekly report, week ending Friday 11 September 2026 - prepared for the Tidewater observability migration (the project this report tracks), with short notes on sister workstreams.

Summary of the week
The Tidewater team spent most of the week on the last third of the service inventory. Of the 142 services in scope, 96 now emit metrics and traces through the new OpenTelemetry collectors, and their old StatsD exporters have been switched off. On-call engineers say the new dashboards load noticeably faster, and the noisy disk-pressure alert that paged the storage team every night has been retuned.

Workstream: collector rollout
Hamid finished the Helm chart changes for the remaining clusters on Tuesday. Canary collectors ran in eu-west for 48 hours with no dropped spans. Memory use per collector pod is about 30 percent lower than the vendor estimate, so we will not need the larger node pool we had pencilled in.

Workstream: data retention and storage
This is where the week went sideways. The remaining 46 services are all inside the payments and identity domains, and those domains fall under the PCI scope. Security informed us on Wednesday that no telemetry from PCI-scoped services may be shipped to the new storage backend until the backend passes its quarterly PCI assessment, and the assessor has not yet confirmed when the review will take place. Without that sign-off we cannot point a single one of those 46 services at the new collectors, and there is no partial path: the old exporters cannot be decommissioned and the migration cannot be closed out. Asha has sent the evidence pack to the assessor and is asking daily for a review slot; nobody on the team can do anything further on those services in the meantime.

Workstream: dashboards and alert parity
Lucia's group rebuilt 61 of the 70 critical dashboards. The remaining nine belong to the services stuck behind the PCI review, so they cannot be validated against real traffic yet. Alert-parity testing for the first 96 services is complete, with two thresholds adjusted after a false-positive storm on Monday night.

Sister workstreams (not part of Tidewater)
- The log-sampling experiment run by the SRE guild was cancelled on Thursday after it reduced costs by less than 2 percent; the guild is closing the repository.
- The CI runner upgrade is a week late because the new base image broke two legacy Java builds; the build team expects to finish on September 18.
- Capacity planning for Q4 is on schedule and will be presented at the October all-hands.

Costs
Spend on the new backend this month is tracking 8 percent under budget, mainly because of the lower collector memory footprint. Finance asked for a forecast that includes the remaining services, which Gabriel will provide once their volumes are known.

People
Hamid is on leave from September 21 to 25. Lucia will cover the collector on-call rotation. We welcomed Tobi Adeyemi, who joins from the networking team and will pick up the dashboard backlog.

Next week
Hamid will tidy the Helm repo and remove the old StatsD charts for the 96 migrated services. Lucia will run a second false-positive review. Gabriel will draft the finance forecast.

Today: 2026-11-12
ADR 2026-14: Hybrid lexical-plus-vector retrieval for Saffron search. This decision record belongs to the Saffron project (site search relevance upgrade for the Pantry & Co. recipe platform). Status: accepted on 12 November 2026. Owner: Beatriz Moura. Reviewers: Kofi Mensah, Elena Rossi.

Context
Saffron's goal is to improve the quality of recipe search before the holiday season, when search traffic triples. The success criterion agreed with the business is a 10 percent increase in click-through on the first page of results, measured in an A/B test, with the new ranking live for all users by December 9. That date was chosen so that the new ranking is in place before the Christmas traffic peak begins around December 12.

The current engine is pure BM25 over titles, ingredients and tags. It fails on descriptive queries such as "something warm with leftover rice" and on synonyms like "aubergine" and "eggplant".

Options
1. Tune the BM25 configuration and add a synonym list. Cheap, but offline tests showed only a 3 percent gain.
2. Replace BM25 with dense vector retrieval. Large gain on descriptive queries, but it regressed on exact dish names ("pad thai") and its latency was 2.5 times higher.
3. Hybrid retrieval: run both and merge results with reciprocal-rank fusion, then rerank the top 50 with a small cross-encoder.

Decision
We adopt option 3.

Evidence
Offline evaluation on 4,000 judged queries: option 3 improved nDCG@10 by 14 percent over production, compared with 3 percent for option 1 and 9 percent for option 2. P95 latency is 180 ms, within the 250 ms budget, after we moved the cross-encoder to the GPU nodes the recommendations team released in October.

Delivery
The embedding pipeline indexed all 310,000 recipes on November 6 and refreshes nightly. The A/B test has been running at 10 percent of traffic since November 9; after three days the treatment arm shows a 12 percent click-through lift, and the test is planned to run until November 23 for significance. Ramp-up to 100 percent is scheduled for December 2, a week before the December 9 date, and the remaining tasks (dashboard, alerting, runbook) are each under two days of work. The rollback switch has been rehearsed twice.

Consequences
We take on a second index to maintain, and a GPU dependency for reranking. If the GPU nodes are unavailable, the system falls back to the fused results without reranking, which in testing still beat production by 9 percent.

Related work outside Saffron
- The meal-planner team's plan to build its own semantic search was cancelled in favour of calling Saffron's API after launch.
- The ingredient-substitution feature is two sprints behind because the nutrition database licence renewal is late; it does not touch search.
- The mobile team is waiting on app-store review for a release that changes the search bar placeholder text; that change is cosmetic and independent of ranking.

Open questions
Should we expose "why this result" explanations to users? Design will explore it in Q1. Do we need per-locale embeddings for the Spanish site? Probably, but the Spanish site is outside Saffron's scope this year.

Revisit
This ADR will be revisited after the A/B test concludes or if latency exceeds budget for more than a day.

Today: 2026-11-06
PRD - Atlas Payroll: Germany and Netherlands expansion. Milestone edition of 6 November 2026. This PRD is for the Atlas DE/NL expansion; other Atlas roadmap items appear only in the dependency list.

1. Goal
Let mid-sized employers already using Atlas for UK payroll run German and Dutch payroll in the same product, so they no longer need a separate local provider. Target customers: 140 existing UK clients with staff in Germany or the Netherlands, of whom 38 signed letters of intent.

2. Scope
- Gross-to-net calculation for Germany (income tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax, social insurance) and the Netherlands (wage tax, national insurance, employee insurance).
- Electronic filing: ELSTER wage-tax returns and DEUEV social-insurance notifications in Germany; payroll tax returns to the Dutch tax authority.
- Payslips in German, Dutch and English.
- Year-end certificates (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung, jaaropgaaf).

3. Original plan
Calculation engines complete by the end of September, filing integrations certified in November, general availability on January 15, 2027, so that customers could start with the first payroll of the new tax year.

4. Progress
Germany calculation engine: complete, verified against 2,400 test cases supplied by our tax advisers, all matching to the cent.
Netherlands calculation engine: complete except the 30-percent ruling for expat employees, due next sprint.
Payslip templates: complete in all three languages.

5. Filing certification and revised dates
The ELSTER certification failed its first round in October because our test transmissions used an outdated XML schema version for the wage-tax return. The fix took the team a week, but the tax authority only runs certification rounds monthly and the next available slot is December 8. The DEUEV certification also has to be repeated afterwards because it depends on the same employer master data. With both rounds, German filing cannot be certified before mid-January, so general availability moves from January 15 to March 2, 2027, and the first German payrolls will run from March. The Netherlands filing integration is not affected and continues in parallel; the engineering team is using the gap to finish the 30-percent ruling and to build the year-end certificate generator early. Sales has informed the 38 letter-of-intent customers of the March date; two asked for a call, none withdrew.

6. Dependencies
- Atlas identity platform: SSO for the new country modules is live since October.
- Atlas Benefits marketplace: paused by leadership while pricing is reviewed; it does not touch payroll calculation.
- Atlas Spain expansion: cancelled in August after the partner firm withdrew. No shared code beyond the localisation library.
- Bank-file generation for SEPA: delivered by the payments team in September.

7. Metrics
Calculation accuracy is 100 percent on the advisers' test set. Performance: 10,000 payslips in 3 minutes 40 seconds, within the 5-minute target.

8. Risks
Tax rules for 2027 will be published in December in both countries; the rule-update process has been rehearsed with the 2026 mid-year changes. Customer onboarding needs local bank details for each employee, and some clients may be slow to collect them.

NET-3302 Bramble: move all customer-facing DNS zones from LegacyHost to the new managed DNS provider. This ticket is the Bramble project; tickets from other infrastructure work are linked at the bottom for context only.

Owner: Ilse Vandenberg | Reporter: Gareth Pugh (Infrastructure lead) | Due: 20 Mar 2026 | Priority: P1

Why
The LegacyHost contract ends on March 20. After that date LegacyHost stops answering queries for our zones, which would take down bramble.shop, the payments subdomain and the partner API. Bramble moves 14 zones (about 2,300 records) to the new provider, including DNSSEC re-signing, and transfers the bramble.shop registration away from LegacyHost's reseller account.

Plan (from 9 Feb)
1. Export zones and validate records - Feb 13.
2. Recreate zones at the new provider, compare answers with a diff tool - Feb 27.
3. Transfer the domain registration and switch nameservers - Mar 6.
4. DNSSEC key rollover to the new provider's keys - Mar 10 to 13.
5. Decommission LegacyHost records - Mar 16.

Comment - Ilse, 13 Feb
Export complete. Found 41 stale records pointing at retired load balancers; removed them after checking with the owning teams.

Comment - Ilse, 26 Feb
All 14 zones recreated at the new provider. The diff tool shows identical answers for every record except two TXT records with different quoting, which resolve the same way. Health checks configured.

Comment - Gareth, 2 Mar
Reminder that the payments subdomain must not drop even for a minute; the payment provider caches failures for an hour.

Comment - Ilse, 5 Mar
The domain transfer is stuck. LegacyHost's reseller placed a transfer lock on bramble.shop and requires the original account holder's written authorisation to release it; the account was opened in 2014 by a director who left the company, and the reseller will not accept a letter from anyone else without notarised proof of authority. Legal has started that paperwork but cannot say how long the notary and the reseller's review will take. Until the lock is released we cannot transfer the registration or change the nameservers, and steps 4 and 5 both depend on the nameserver switch, so nothing further can move.

Comment - Tom Achebe (Legal), 9 Mar
Notarised documents requested from the company secretary. No response from the reseller yet on what format they accept.

Comment - Gareth, 10 Mar
Asked LegacyHost whether they can extend the contract beyond March 20 as a safety net. Awaiting reply.
